v84: FAILS - hermesc rejects the `class` keyword entirely: "invalid statement
     encountered" pointing at the class declaration itself. This is not a
     parser limitation (Hermes's parser accepts and produces a full AST for
     class syntax, verified with `hermesc -dump-ast`) -- it is IRGen: this
     hermesc build (hermes-engine-cli@0.8.1, HBC v84) has no lowering at all
     for ClassDeclaration/ClassExpression nodes to bytecode. Confirmed with
     minimal repros (`class C {}`, `class C { method(){} }`,
     `class C extends D {}`) -- all fail identically regardless of body
     contents.
v94: FAILS - identical "invalid statement encountered" error, same root cause
     (react-native@0.72.17's bundled hermesc also lacks class lowering in
     IRGen).
v99: OK - hermes-compiler@260318099.0.1 fully supports `class` (including
     this construct's accessors/inheritance/fields as applicable).

Only v99.hbc exists in this directory; tests/fixtures/build.sh skips v84/v94
for this fixture, matching this file. Historically, React Native's Metro/Babel
pipeline transpiled all class syntax to ES5 prototype chains before handing
JS to Hermes in this era, which is presumably why hermesc itself never grew
class-lowering support until some commit between HBC v94 and v99.
